issues.description: Real-time pacing claimed in docstring/changelog but not implemented
issues.detail: The PR description and the new fixed_audio_packet_size docstring promise 'real-time pacing' for endpoints like Vonage Audio Connector, but the implementation only does fixed-size chunking. _write_frame immediately flushes every full chunk via _client.send in a tight while loop without consulting _send_interval/_next_send_time. Bursts of large payloads will be sent back-to-back, overflowing the remote jitter buffer. Either implement actual pacing using the existing _next_send_time machinery on the class, or remove the 'real-time pacing' claim from the docstring/changelog.

issues.description: fixed_audio_packet_size lacks validation against sample-width alignment
issues.detail: The parameter is documented as '640 for 20ms @ 16kHz PCM16 mono' but nothing checks that the buffered bytes split cleanly on sample boundaries. Zero, negative, or non-multiple-of-sample-width values produce undefined behavior: 0 silently disables the feature, negative loops forever, an odd value slices mid-sample and produces garbage forever (no resync). Validate at setup that packet_bytes > 0 and is a multiple of bytes-per-sample-frame, or express the parameter in samples/milliseconds and compute bytes internally.

issues.description: Packetization path treats every bytes payload as audio, will corrupt non-audio binary frames
issues.detail: _write_frame checks isinstance(payload, (bytes, bytearray)) to decide whether to apply fixed_audio_packet_size chunking. Any serializer is free to return bytes for non-audio frames (control messages, framed binary protocols, Opus packets, future frame types) — splitting such a payload at an audio-frame boundary will corrupt it silently. Gate on the source frame type (e.g. isinstance(frame, AudioRawFrame)) rather than on payload type, or have the serializer tag audio output explicitly. The 'payload is raw PCM at a known width' precondition is unstated and unenforced.

issues.description: Trailing partial buffer is silently dropped on session end / disconnect
issues.detail: The new send-buffer code holds any remainder smaller than packet_bytes indefinitely. The buffer is only cleared on InterruptionFrame; on EndFrame, disconnect, transport teardown, or normal end-of-utterance, residual bytes (0 to packet_bytes-1) sit in the buffer and will be prepended to the next session's audio, producing a phase-shifted PCM artifact — or are simply lost. State the invariant ('buffer empty at session boundary'), then decide explicitly: pad with silence or drop. Clear on StartFrame and on serializer setup as well.

issues.description: Packetization belongs in the serializer, not the generic transport
issues.detail: Vonage's wire format requires fixed-size PCM packets — that knowledge belongs inside VonageFrameSerializer (it is part of the Vonage protocol contract). Instead, the transport exposes fixed_audio_packet_size as a generic FastAPIWebsocketParams field that the caller must set correctly. A caller wiring Vonage must know an implementation detail (640 bytes = 20ms @ 16kHz PCM16 mono) the abstraction was supposed to hide, and every future framed serializer (Twilio, Plivo, etc.) would force transport changes. Change serialize()'s return shape to allow Iterable[bytes | str], move packet-size knowledge into the serializer, and let the transport stay generic. This also eliminates the InterruptionFrame buffer-clear coupling.

issues.description: FrameSerializer contract is imprecise: serialize() postcondition (one wire message vs stream) is not pinned, weakening substitutability
issues.detail: The abstract FrameSerializer.serialize() implicitly promises 'a serialized payload that the transport sends as-is'. Vonage's implementation returns raw PCM whose size depends on input and resampling ratio, which is why the transport had to add a side-channel buffer. This weakens the implicit postcondition that 'one serialize() output equals one wire message' (LSP violation). Strengthen the supertype contract — allow serialize() to return an iterable of payloads with framing semantics owned by the serializer — or push packetization into the serializer.

issues.description: Audio send buffer mutated without stated invariant; concurrent access and ordering hazards
issues.detail: _audio_send_buffer is a bytearray mutated across calls with no stated invariant ('len(buf) < packet_bytes after each _write_frame returns'). There is no upper bound or backpressure if send() blocks while inputs continue to arrive. If two coroutines ever race _write_frame and process_frame(InterruptionFrame), the clear and extend/del can interleave at await points. Additionally, non-audio payloads (e.g. serialized OutputTransportMessageFrame JSON) bypass the buffer and are emitted immediately while audio sits buffered, silently reshuffling order across modalities. State the invariant in a comment, ensure single-owner access, and either flush the audio buffer before emitting non-audio, or document the reordering.

issues.description: Hot-path bytearray copies are gratuitously expensive
issues.detail: self._audio_send_buffer.extend(bytes(payload)) converts the payload to bytes (copy) then extends (copy). bytes(self._audio_send_buffer[:packet_bytes]) slices (copy) then converts (copy). del self._audio_send_buffer[:packet_bytes] shifts the tail (copy). That's 4-5 copies per packet on an audio fast path running every 20ms. Use a collections.deque of fixed-size chunks plus an index, or a memoryview with periodic compaction. Also compute n = len(buf) // packet_bytes once and slice off n*packet_bytes rather than looping with repeated mutations — the chunker becomes a pure (buffer, payload, size) -> (chunks, remainder) function that is trivially unit-testable.

issues.description: No tests accompany the new serializer or the packetization buffer
issues.detail: There are no unit tests for VonageFrameSerializer.serialize/deserialize (audio resample path, DTMF parsing, JSON dispatch, clear/notify events) and none for the fixed_audio_packet_size buffering (boundary alignment, interruption-clears-buffer, payload-smaller-than-packet, payload-larger-than-2x-packet). The packetization logic is pure, deterministic, and trivial to test without a websocket — exactly the kind of stateful buffering that lands subtle bugs without coverage.

issues.description: DTMF digit parsing accepts two undocumented payload shapes with no source citation
issues.detail: digit = message.get('digit') or message.get('dtmf', {}).get('digit') tries two shapes because the author was unsure which Vonage sends, with no link to the Vonage docs, no test fixture for either, and no precedence rationale. Either pin against the documented Vonage spec and handle one shape (rejecting the other with a clear error), or, if both genuinely exist in the wild, name both variants in a comment with versions and a doc URL. Defensive try-both code rots — a year from now no one will know whether the fallback is still needed.

issues.description: Empty-resample guards duplicated and resampler streaming contract unstated
issues.detail: Both serialize() and deserialize() check `if resampled is None or len(resampled) == 0: return None` with a comment treating the empty case as an error. A streaming resampler legitimately produces zero output bytes for some inputs (insufficient samples to fill an output frame) — this is the normal streaming invariant, not an error. State the resampler's postcondition explicitly: if it buffers internally, the None-return is fine; if not, audio is being discarded. Standardizing on b'' would let one check suffice.

issues.description: InputParams.sample_rate override semantics are ambiguous and unvalidated
issues.detail: self._sample_rate starts at 0 and is only set in setup(). The contract is unclear: does sample_rate override only the input direction, both directions, or the pipeline rate? Currently it is used for the deserialize() output frame's sample_rate, but the output path resamples from frame.sample_rate (the producer's rate) regardless. If serialize/deserialize were ever called before setup(), the resampler would be asked to resample to rate 0. State the precondition explicitly, make it part of an immutable config constructed at setup, and refuse to operate before it exists.

issues.description: Changelog references a rename that does not appear in the diff
issues.detail: The changelog asserts a rename from audio_packet_bytes to fixed_audio_packet_size, but the visible diff only adds fixed_audio_packet_size — the old name is not removed. Either the old name never existed in main (and the changelog is misleading), the removal is elsewhere, or this PR mashes three separate changes (serializer, packetization, rename) into one. Split the patch and reconcile the changelog with the actual diff before merge.

issues.description: Truthy guard `if payload:` conflates None with empty-but-valid bytes
issues.detail: The condition `if payload:` is false for b'', '', and None indiscriminately. The serializer's contract explicitly returns None for 'no frame produced'; the transport should test `if payload is not None` so that an empty-but-valid serialization result is handled per the contract rather than silently dropped. A small fix but exactly the kind of unreasoned shortcut that becomes a heisenbug under a different serializer.

issues.description: deserialize() event dispatch could be a dict; error vs unknown-event semantics conflated
issues.detail: The text-event handling is six if/elif branches that all just log and return None except the DTMF case — a small dict mapping event name to handler would make the data shape obvious and let the DTMF case stand out. Additionally, 'event I do not handle', 'JSON I could not parse', and 'DTMF with invalid digit' all return None, so a caller cannot distinguish benign unknown events from protocol-level failures. Document the postcondition explicitly (None means 'no frame to emit, possibly due to error already logged') or split: raise on malformed JSON, return None on unknown event.

synthesis.summary: The Vonage serializer itself is small and mostly clean, but the patch's core defect is in src/pipecat/transports/websocket/fastapi.py: protocol-level packetization has leaked into the generic transport via fixed_audio_packet_size, and that buffer is under-specified along every axis the panel cares about — no real-time pacing despite the docstring claim, no alignment validation, no flush at session end, no type guard distinguishing PCM from arbitrary bytes, no stated invariant or concurrency model, and 4-5 hot-path copies per packet. The correct fix multiple reviewers converge on is to move packet-size knowledge into the serializer (allow serialize() to return Iterable[bytes | str]) so the transport stays dumb and any framed protocol composes naturally; otherwise, at minimum validate the parameter, implement the advertised pacing or remove the claim, flush on EndFrame/disconnect, and add unit tests for the buffer state machine. Smaller cleanups: the DTMF try-both fallback wants a Vonage-doc citation, the changelog references a rename not present in the diff, the `if payload:` guard should be `is not None`, and the deserialize event chain wants a dispatch dict with clearer error-vs-unknown semantics.
